SMTO-GWT-0078 — SMTO couldn't understand this GPU request

GUID: 9cbae590-0438-5f58-83b6-ffe80264664e
Slug: gpu-invalid-request
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO's GPU skill only accepts a fixed set of actions, each with specific details. This request didn't fit one of them, or went to a different computer than intended, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again, naming the GPU by its number or ID and giving exact values, for example "set GPU 0's power limit to 250 watts". Each GPU action needs specific details, such as which card and which value, before SMTO will run it.
  2. Stick to what the GPU skill offers: readings, processes, power limit, persistence mode, compute mode, clock ranges and reset. Don't ask for custom NVIDIA command options. SMTO doesn't pass made-up NVIDIA command options to the card, so such requests are always refused.
  3. Make sure the Gateway chosen for this conversation is the computer that has the GPU. A GPU request that reaches a different Gateway than the one it was prepared for is refused.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the GPU action and reports its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to get around this by asking SMTO to run NVIDIA commands directly.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GPU admission rejected the request: unknown operation, request node not matching the Gateway's node name, arguments failing the operation's schema or type checks, or a compiled nvidia-smi argv outside the allowed read/configuration grammar.

What this means

  • GPU admission rejected an unknown operation, wrong node, invalid typed arguments or a generated provider command outside the allowed read/configuration classes. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • GPU admission rejected an unknown operation, wrong node, invalid typed arguments or a generated provider command outside the allowed read/configuration classes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare operation and argument types with the discovered schema, including finite numeric values and device-bound expected_uuid.

How to fix it

  • Compare the tool call with the gpu.* operation schemas (SPECS/SCHEMAS in src/gateway_core/gpu/models.py): valid operation name, device as an index or GPU-... UUID, expected_uuid only with device, integer MHz values and finite numbers. Confirm the request's node matches the selected Gateway's node_name; arbitrary NVIDIA arguments are not supported.
  • Use the discovered GPU schema; arbitrary NVIDIA arguments are not supported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the discovered GPU schema; arbitrary NVIDIA arguments are not supported.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended typed request validates for the correct node without arbitrary provider arguments.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
